proof.criterion: The install lock's wait is bounded, so a stalled holder costs one bump its launch rather than making every role of the pod wait past the registration deadline.
proof.surface: The rendered install script itself, run against a cache directory a holder process holds the lock on, in this issue's pod; the bound rendered as `-w 1` for the measurement so the run is quick, and the pre-fix shape (no `-w`) run beside it as the control.
proof.command: setsid /usr/bin/flock -- cache sh -c 'sleep 12' & then: sh install-w1.sh /bin/echo AGENT-EXECED   and   timeout 5 sh install-nowait.sh /bin/echo AGENT-EXECED
proof.observed: Bounded: exit=1 after 2.03 s — two waits of the bound — with `legion plugins: installing @sjawhar/pi-legion@10.14.0 and @sjawhar/pi-envoy@10.12.0 failed` on stderr and the agent argv never exec'd. Unbounded (today's shape without the flag): still blocked when `timeout 5` killed it, exit=124 at 5.01 s, no output. The mechanism was confirmed before the bound was chosen, the way the reviewer found the defect: a bare `flock` waiter on a held directory under `timeout 3` exits 124 at 3.01 s where `flock -w 2` exits 1 at 2.00 s, so flock excludes on a directory and really did wait forever.
proof.negativeControl: The unbounded run is the control: same rendered script, same holder, same cache, one flag apart — it hangs where the bounded one fails loudly.

proof.criterion: Two rendered installs of one pod actually serialise on the shared bun cache, rather than the script merely containing the word flock.
proof.surface: `TestTwoRenderedInstallsSerialiseOnTheSharedBunCache` in packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox: two rendered scripts, one role state home each, one shared BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR, run concurrently with a stand-in bun — substituted at the script's absolute bun path by the same strings.Replace bunInstallArgs already used, so no production signature widened — that logs `start <id>`, holds 300 ms, logs `end <id>`.
proof.observed: PASS in 1.19 s; ten runs `ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox 11.912s` with no flake. With installLockWaitSeconds mutated to 0 the test fails — `the locked run's log: the log is not two completed installs: ["start a" "end a"]` — and TestTheInstallLockWaitIsABoundTwoOfWhichFitTheRegistrationDeadline fails with `installLockWaitSeconds = 0, want a positive bound`, while every substring assertion over the script still passes; restored, both green. With `-w` removed entirely the test still passes, which is right: an unbounded lock still serialises, and the bound is the other test's job.
proof.negativeControl: Built into the test and run every time: the identical harness with the rendered flock prefix stripped must interleave, and a control that fails to interleave in five attempts is a t.Fatal saying the locked run passed vacuously — so a harness that never exercised concurrency can never look green.

proof.criterion: The lock's binary is declared where the image's other tools are, so an image without it fails the build rather than every installing launch.
proof.surface: The `toolchain` capability row `legion probe-image` asserts (packages/daemon/internal/capabilities), exercised through its own suite with the stub PATH the capability tests build.
proof.command: go test -count=1 ./internal/capabilities/... , then the same with "flock" removed from capabilitiestest's stub binaries, then restored
proof.observed: Green as it stands (`ok … 23.507s`). With the stub removed: `capability toolchain is missing: flock is not on PATH` from deployment_test.go:45 and image_test.go:104 and :159. Restored: green again. The apt line now names `util-linux` with the reason beside it, and the Dockerfile's toolchain check runs `flock --version`.
proof.negativeControl: The stub removal above is the control; before this round the same removal changed nothing, since no list looked for flock.

proof.criterion: The lock rather than the retry is what removes the cold-fill failures — the question this implementer's own before/after could not answer.
proof.surface: The tester's own control, recorded in .legion/INFRA-31/test.json round nine and cited here by name rather than re-derived: the rendered script with flock removed and the retry kept, run six-way cold in the tester's container.
proof.command: the tester's rendered six-way cold run with the flock prefix stripped and `legion_install || legion_install` left in place
proof.observed: 2 of 6 failed both attempts on its first cold run, and the second run passed only with `ENOENT: failed copying files from cache to destination` in two roles' logs, succeeding on the retry. So the retry alone masks the race sometimes and not always; with the lock in place the tester's four post-fix cold runs were 6 of 6 exit 0 with ENOENT absent from every log.
proof.negativeControl: The tester's pre-fix cold runs (4 of 6 and 2 of 6 failing, no failing role reaching its exec) are the control for the post-fix runs; the flock-removed, retry-kept run is the control that separates the lock from the retry.

docs/kubernetes.md — the bun paragraph now says the wait is bounded, what the bound is sized against and what a timeout does, with the scoped chalk/lodash measurement left exactly as it was; the two operator-facing toolchain lists, the Dockerfile-step list and the `docker run` end-to-end check name flock.
trickyParts: The bound is one number serving two opposing constraints, which is why the constant's comment shows the arithmetic rather than asserting a value: two timed-out waits (the script installs twice) must fit inside the 360 s registration deadline with room for the install and the agent's start, and the bound must still cover the legitimate case where the last of six roles queues behind five serialised installs. 120 s satisfies both: 2 x 120 = 240 < 360, and 120 s allows those five installs 24 s each.

`installScript` calls bun by absolute path, so a stub cannot be put on PATH. The way past it was already in the file: bunInstallArgs substitutes the stub for `/usr/local/bin/bun` with strings.Replace on the rendered text. That keeps the rendered script — the lock included — as the thing under test and widens no production signature, which the alternatives (parameterising the bun path, or testing a hand-built lock construct) would have done.

A serialisation assertion can pass vacuously when the second process merely starts after the first finishes, so the test runs its own lockless control in the same invocation and fails if that control never interleaves.
deviations: The reviewer filed the behavioural serialisation test as fast-follow; the architect asked for it in this round and it is here, with its control. Nothing else was taken from the fast-follow list.
discoveredComplexity: `flock` with no `-w` waits without limit, which converts a per-role failure into a pod-wide one as soon as several roles share a lock: the amplification is a property of the lock, not of bun, and it was found by measuring the mechanism (a holder-and-waiter rig) rather than by reading the diff.
